paper_id: Xue et al. - 2005 - Access Control Policy Negotiation for Remote Hot-deployed Grid Services
title: Access Control Policy Negotiation for Remote Hot-deployed Grid Services
motivation: Grid services have deployers and containers in different autonomous domains, so access control cannot be determined unilaterally.
problem_framing: How to jointly determine access control policy for a remotely deployed grid service when neither deployer nor container owns both service and resources.
key_insight: Use three types of rule-based meta-policies (proposal making, combining algorithm selection, validity checking) to automate policy negotiation between deployers and containers.
method_signature: Non-recursive stratified Datalog with constraints policy language + meta-policy controlled negotiation procedure
evaluation_criteria: Negotiation time vs policy size parameters and concurrent request count in CROWN Grid deployment
negative_result_or_admitted_limitation: Worst-case validation query evaluation is at least co-NP-hard; we do not see any single combining algorithm suitable for all grid conflicts.
evidence_for_taste: existing grid deployment solutions do not address this unique requirement
cannot be determined by the deployer or the container only
we do not see any single combining algorithm suitable
the worst-case complexity is at least co-NP hard
most cases are simple according to our experiences
the deployer and container owner usually concern with different authorization factors
thinking_moves: Identifies unique requirement absent from existing grid solutions
Acknowledges theoretical intractability then argues practical tractability
Distinguishes deployer concerns (user identity) from container concerns (raw resources)
Proposes meta-policies over single fixed algorithm to handle heterogeneity
